newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of India sounds out firms for IPO subscription.
newsitem.headline: Bank of India sounds out firms for IPO subscription.

text.p: The state-run Bank of India is seeking support from corporates for its 6.75 billion rupee initial public offering (IPO) of shares, company officials said.
"We have received a letter from them (the Bank of India) about the issue," an executive at one of India's top private firms said.
He said Bank of India officials were also seeking an appointment with top finance executives of his company.
Another state-run bank's IPO late last year was bailed out by large companies, many of whom happened to be the bank's clients, analysts said.
P.S. Shenoy, Bank of India's general manager in charge of the public issue, said there was no question of any coercion.
"Yes, we have written to some old friends, our customers and some non-customers," Shenoy said. "But it is just a request."
"We are informing them about the issue. They should not later say we were not told," Shenoy said.
"But we are not doing it on a large scale," he said.
"The bank's focus was the small investor," he added.
Shenoy said he expected the issue to be oversubscribed 2.5 times, based on feedback he received at a meeting of brokers selling the issue on Thursday.
Bank of India is issuing 10 rupees face value shares at 45 rupees each to raise 6.75 billion rupees.
The bank said it recorded a net profit of 2.76 billion rupees in 1995/96 (April-March).
Bank of India's maiden share issue opens on February 21.
